 Local farm stand accepts SNAP benefits 
 Open Audio Article Player 
 By ops@our-hometown.com 
 on 
 November 04, 2026 
 LEADER STAFF 
 NEWS@PTLEADER.COM 
 A customer uses the self-checkout kiosk at Red Dog Farm in Chimacum. Red Dog Farm is the first farm on the Olympic Peninsula to accept SNAP benefits at its farm stand. Photo courtesy of Rodney Just/Red Dog Farm
 Red Dog Farm, an organic vegetable farm in Chimacum, is now accepting Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits for eligible food items at its newly renovated and expanded self-service farm stand.
 The farm began accepting SNAP benefits in late September. It operates on an honor system and offers more than produce.
 Seasonal vegetables, plant starts and fruit are accompanied by baked goods, pantry staples, meat, eggs, cheese and other regional products.
 A new automated self-checkout system allows customers to pay by card, including eligible EBT cards used to access SNAP benefits.
 “We’ve been exploring ways to increase food access in our community, and we’re thrilled to announce that we can now accept SNAP benefits year-round for our fresh produce and other locally sourced foods,” farm owner Karyn Williams said. “This is a much-needed step toward making fresh, local, and organic foods more accessible and affordable for everyone in our community. We believe everyone deserves access to nourishing, high-quality food, and we’re excited to make that a little easier for more families.”
 The farm stand’s renovation and expansion, along with the improvements that made SNAP acceptance possible, were supported by two grants from the Washington State Department of Agriculture in 2025 and 2026.
 The Red Dog Farm and farm stand, 406 Center Road, Chimacum, is open every day, year-round from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.
